title: staggered-policy-rollout-led-to-region-mismatch-and-quantized-model-swap
creator: Priya Rao
description: Summary: On 2026-03-05 we received multiple customer escalations reporting elevated latency and degraded output quality for requests originating from EU tenants. Investigation showed requests that should have routed to the EU-hosted model pool were consistently routed to a US-based quantized variant. Impact: Affected ~12 customers (mid-market + enterprise tenants) for ~2.5 hours during peak traffic windows, resulting in higher tail latency and an increase in tokenization/formatting regressions for some prompt shapes. Root cause hypothesis: A staggered rollout of a policy delta (policy TTL and priority reordering) was applied with an incorrect merge order in the policy-sync job. The sync job applies deltas in chunks to reduce lock contention; one chunk applied an older-priority policy after a newer delta, producing a transient policy state where region affinity weights for certain tenant tags were inverted. This transient state persisted in the routing cache long enough for requests to be matched against a compat/quantized variant in the US. Reproduction: 1) Create tenant with eu-region affinity tag and a small dedicated capacity tag. 2) Apply a staggered policy rollout with chunk size 3 and force a sync interruption mid-chunk. 3) Observe route evaluation against stale merged policy and route to incompatible variant. Immediate mitigations applied: - Rollback of the rollout (2026-03-05 11:47 UTC) which stopped further misroutes. - Purge of policy evaluation cache across regional routers (2026-03-05 12:03 UTC). - Short-term hotfix: Disable chunked-merge path for policy-sync until fix is deployed. Permanent fix plan: 1) Fix policy-sync to guarantee monotonic merge order (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/789). 2) Add atomic swap for policy blobs in service discovery layer so rollouts are applied atomically per-region (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Atomic+Policy+Swaps). 3) Add end-to-end integration tests that simulate interrupted syncs and validate route stability. 4) Improve observability: add a policy-delta-apply metric and alert when merge-order anomalies occur (dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/incident-193827). Communications: Customer outreach thread created (CRM tickets: CRM-5512, CRM-5519). Postmortem page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-193827-postmortem. Stakeholders: SRE, Routing, Dedicated infra, Customer Success. Timeline: 2026-03-05 10:12 UTC - first alert; 10:25 UTC - on-call bridge; 11:47 UTC - rollback; 12:03 UTC - cache purge; 14:50 UTC - customer notifications sent. Next steps: complete PR review and deploy runtime-1.22 patch, release postmortem, and follow up with a dedicated traffic replay to validate fixes in staging.

2026-03-05 12:10 UTC - Marco Silva (SRE): Cache purge completed. Confirmed no further EU->US quantized routes appearing in the last 30m across sample tenants.
2026-03-06 09:05 UTC - Design Review (Liam O'Connor): Requested design doc for atomic swap and formal verification plan for merge order. Assigned to Routing team.
